newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst plans new biotech research activity.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst plans new biotech research activity.

text.p: German chemical giant Hoechst AG said on Wednesday it planned to set up a small biotechnology research facility near Munich that would also cover the field of genetics.

A Hoechst spokesman, responding to a telephone enquiry, said around 20 researchers would be employed in rented premises there but denied a magazine report that the concern had plans to build a full biotechnology centre.

German magazine Wirtschaftswoche said in a pre-release of an article to appear on Thursday that Hoechst would be restarting genetics research in the new premises after four years absence from Germany.

It said Hoechst had moved its genetics research activities to the U.S. following resistance it encountered from local government authorities in Hesse, the region in which its Frankfurt head offices are based.
The magazine quoted a Hoechst executive as saying that co-operation with German authorities had since improved.

The Hoechst spokesman refused to confirm the quotes but when asked if the planned activities would include genetics research, he replied that the Munich team would be looking at all aspects of biotechnology.
